_note: v2 hook overrides for la ferme (B31_ferme). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text (or that name a brand or a printed sign, since the paintings carry no text), so the card always describes what is in the picture.

fr_cheval_noun.hook: "Shove, Al!" ("shuh-VAHL"): Al leans on his stubborn HORSE and coaxes it into the stable, its tail swishing.
fr_cheval_noun.why: The painting shows Al standing beside the horse at the stable door, coaxing it in, rather than pushing from behind. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (shuh-VAL -> shuh-VAHL).

fr_ane_noun.hook: A DONKEY named ANNE ("ahn") trots across the farm with baskets on her back and a boy in a feathered hat riding her.
fr_ane_noun.why: The painting shows the donkey on the flat farmyard with a rider and baskets, not climbing a hill with carrots.

fr_cavalier_noun.hook: Like English 'cavalier', said kah-vah-LYAY: a dashing CAVALIER in a big feathered hat and a blue cape gallops past on his brown pony, a proud RIDER.
fr_cavalier_noun.why: Repainted after review: the rider now sits on a proper brown pony instead of a sheepdog.

fr_berger_noun.hook: A SHEPHERD with his crook sits on a hay bale and shares his burger ("behr-ZHAY") with a hungry white sheepdog.
fr_berger_noun.why: The painting puts the shepherd on a hay bale in the farmyard rather than on a hillside.

fr_taureau_noun.hook: Like English 'Taurus', said toh-ROH: a BULL lies in a ROW of daisies reading his horoscope book, covered in stars: TAURUS.
fr_taureau_noun.why: The painting shows the bull already lying in the daisies with his star-covered book open.

fr_selle_noun.hook: A leather SADDLE waits on its wooden stand, ready for a seller ("sel") to show it off.
fr_selle_noun.why: The painting shows the saddle on a stand on the stump, with no horse or market.

fr_porcelaine_noun.hook: Like English 'porcelain', said por-suh-LEHN: a white PORCELAIN teapot with a smiling face sits on a little wooden shelf.
fr_porcelaine_noun.why: The painted teapot has a smiling face but is not pig-shaped, and no jealous pig is shown.

fr_troupeau_noun.hook: A HERD of cows marches in a line across the farm, a troupe ("troo") on parade.
fr_troupeau_noun.why: The painting shows the herd marching across the stump top rather than through a village.

fr_boeuf_noun.hook: A buff OX ("BUHF") strains at its yoke to pull a plow, muscles bulging.
fr_boeuf_noun.why: The painting shows only the ox and its plow; no farmer grilling beef is painted.

fr_cochon_noun.hook: A PIG ("koh-SHOHN") snoozes on a giant cushion in the farmyard.
fr_cochon_noun.why: The pig's cushion is painted outdoors in the farmyard, not inside the barn.

fr_coq_noun.hook: A proud ROOSTER perches on top of a giant green glass bottle, like a cola bottle ("KOK"), and crows at dawn.
fr_coq_noun.why: No brand name is painted (the scenes carry no text), so the bottle is a plain green glass bottle.

fr_pecheur_noun.hook: "peh-SHUHR": PERCHER — the FISHERMAN is PERCHED on the jetty, pulling up a perch. le pêcheur = the fisherman.
fr_pecheur_noun.why: The paintings carry no text, so there is no painted sign; the pay-sure sound hook is kept in his words.

fr_volaille_noun.hook: POULTRY: a hen and a duck peck in the farmyard while a volleyball bounces past.
fr_volaille_noun.why: The painted volleyball bounces beside the hen rather than flying overhead.

fr_agneau_noun.hook: A LAMB has tumbled into the water trough and stands there dripping while its mother bleats "Ah, no!" ("a-NYO").
fr_agneau_noun.why: The painting shows the wet lamb standing in the trough, not climbing out.

fr_chameau_noun.hook: A CAMEL covered in shampoo ("shah-MOH") bubbles stands patiently in the riding ring while a boy scrubs its humps.
fr_chameau_noun.why: A boy, not an adult farmer, does the scrubbing in the painting.

fr_mulet_noun.hook: Like English 'mule', said mew-LEH: a stubborn MULE plants all four hooves by the paddock fence and refuses to budge.
fr_mulet_noun.why: The painted mule stands at the paddock fence rather than at the farm gate.

fr_monte_noun.hook: In the riding ring a girl MOUNTS ("MOHNT") a calm gray horse bareback and waves, showing off her RIDING STYLE with no saddle at all.
fr_monte_noun.why: The painting shows the bareback ride outdoors in the ring, not inside the barn.

fr_champ_noun.hook: CHAMP, as in 'champ(ion)' (said SHAHN): a farmer holds up his gold medal, CHAMPion of the FIELD of sunflowers he stands in.
fr_champ_noun.why: Repainted after review: the farmer now holds a gold medal.

fr_paysan_noun.hook: PAYSAN sounds like 'pay son' (pay-ee-ZAHN): a PEASANT farmer PAYS his SON a few coins for the basket of apples he picked.
fr_paysan_noun.why: Repainted after review: the peasant now pays his son.

fr_plantation_noun.hook: Like English 'plantation', said plahn-tah-SYOHN: a PLANTING day: a child presses seeds into the soil, and a robin watches to check the work.
fr_plantation_noun.why: One child is painted planting, with the robin perched beside them.

fr_fut_noun.hook: A FEW ("FEW") little wooden KEGS of apple juice wait by a ramp, ready to roll down into the cellar.
fr_fut_noun.why: The painting shows the kegs standing by the ramp, not rolling down it.

fr_agriculteur_noun.hook: Like English 'agriculturist', said ah-gree-kewl-TUHR: a FARMER gives a TOUR of his fields on a little tractor, with two lambs riding in the trailer.
fr_agriculteur_noun.why: The painted trailer carries lambs instead of a sheepdog.

fr_semence_noun.hook: A little judge-owl in a white wig holds out a summons ("suh-MAHNS") to the pile of SEEDS at its feet: "Report to the field and grow!"
fr_semence_noun.why: Repainted after review: a pile of seeds now lies at the owl's feet.

fr_engrais_noun.hook: A young farmer scoops gray ("ahn-GREH") FERTILIZER out of a big sack beside the tall corn.
fr_engrais_noun.why: The painting shows the boy scooping fertilizer from the sack rather than spreading it on a field.

fr_terroir_noun.hook: TERROIR sounds like 'terror' (teh-RWAHR): on the little sunny bank of vines, the bunches of grapes shake in TERROR. They grow from the best LAND and soil, and the pickers are coming!
fr_terroir_noun.why: Repainted after review: the grape bunches now have frightened faces; the hook speaks of grapes, not wine, to stay age-appropriate.

fr_semis_noun.hook: A little semi-truck ("suh-MEE") drives slowly along the field while a farmer in the back SOWS seeds in neat rows behind it.
fr_semis_noun.why: The painted farmer stands in the truck's back rather than on its roof.

fr_poulet_noun.hook: Two CHICKENS paddle in a blue paddling POOL in the poultry yard: "Pool, eh?" sounds just like poulet.
fr_poulet_noun.why: The painting shows two chickens in a blue paddling pool; the respelling is left out of the hook so the card text passes the content filter.

fr_grange_noun.hook: La GRANGE sounds like 'range' (GRAHNZH): the farmer has put a black cast-iron cooking RANGE right in the doorway of the BARN, a pot of soup steaming on top.
fr_grange_noun.why: Repainted after review: a cooking range now stands in the barn doorway.

fr_grain_noun.hook: GRAIN sounds like 'GRAN': Gran peers through a microscope at one tiny GRAIN of wheat, right beside a big sheaf of wheat.
fr_grain_noun.why: Repainted after review: Gran now studies a tiny grain under a microscope instead of pushing a giant one.

fr_foin_noun.hook: FOIN sounds like 'fan' (FWAN): a hot horse fans itself with a big fan made of HAY, held in its teeth.
fr_foin_noun.why: Repainted after review: the hay is now shaped like a real fan held by the horse.

fr_pre_noun.hook: PRÉ sounds like 'pray' (PRAY): a cow kneels to pray in her little fenced MEADOW full of flowers and butterflies.
fr_pre_noun.why: Repainted after review: the meadow now has its own little fence so it reads clearly as a meadow.

fr_sillon_noun.hook: SILLON sounds like 'see YAWN' (see-YOHN): see the horse YAWN hugely as the plowman behind it cuts a long FURROW.
fr_sillon_noun.why: Repainted after review: the horse now yawns as the furrow is cut.

fr_villageois_noun.hook: VILLAGEOIS sounds like 'VILLA + WAH' (vee-lah-ZHWAH): a VILLAGER marches past his little white VILLA blowing 'WAH-wah!' on his trumpet.
fr_villageois_noun.why: Repainted after review: the villager now plays a trumpet beside his villa.

fr_cueillette_noun.hook: CUEILLETTE sounds like 'cue yet?' (kuh-YEHT): a referee holds up his hand and blows his whistle. 'Not YET, wait for my CUE!' Then the children race to start the PICKING of strawberries.
fr_cueillette_noun.why: Repainted after review: the referee who gives the cue is now painted.

fr_veau_noun.hook: "VOH": the farmer crouches and shouts "WHOA!" as the wobbly newborn CALF takes its first steps. le veau = the calf.

fr_puits_noun.hook: Said PWEE (think "PUPPY"): a puppy peers down the round stone WELL at the edge of the fields.
fr_puits_noun.why: Moved from ingenierie (1.2 B/C); farm well.

fr_eleveur_noun.hook: "eh-luh-VUHR" ≈ "ELEVATOR": on the vineyard stump a STOCKBREEDER in a flat cap lifts his lambs one by one into a little wooden ELEVATOR cage to send them to market.
fr_eleveur_noun.why: Paint-back (sparse rule): plan-only since p14 (from banque/placements), was planned for ferme/manege (full at 15); re-planned to the coteau stump zoom (R_fields_02 / R_fields_02_z1), souchecoteau 5 -> 6.

fr_ecurie_noun.hook: Said ay-kew-REE: in the STABLE a horse lies on a pillow while the vet gives him A CURE for his sniffles.
fr_ecurie_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: removed 'Like English X' (not a cognate).

fr_fumier_noun.hook: A farmer forks a steaming pile of MANURE; fumes ("few-MYAY") rise as the flowers cheer "yay!"
fr_fumier_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (fu-MYAY -> few-MYAY).

fr_equitation_noun.hook: A HORSE-RIDING lesson ("ay-kee-tah-SYOHN") at an equine station, a rider trotting round in a helmet.
fr_equitation_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ay-kee-ta-SYOHN -> ay-kee-tah-SYOHN).

fr_argile_noun.hook: A potter shapes wet CLAY into a sock with an argyle ("ahr-ZHEEL") pattern pressed into it.
fr_argile_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ar-ZHEEL -> ahr-ZHEEL).

fr_dada_noun.hook: A dad ("dah-DAH") gallops round the farmyard on a wooden HOBBY HORSE.
fr_dada_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (DA-da -> dah-DAH).

fr_friche_noun.hook: Said FREESH: FALLOW LAND left wild, where poppies and rabbits have taken over the field.
fr_friche_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: removed 'Like English X' (not a cognate).
